text:
jordan: Quick Q — RFC follow-up: for Private customers, should controlplane separation force per-tenant egress IPs by default, or keep a shared egress NAT with tenant taggables? I'm worried about auditability vs operational scale.
alyssa: my vote is per-tenant by default for compliance customers. Audit logs + external allowlists make that so much easier.
kevin: per-tenant is nice but ENI/route table limits in accounts will explode at scale. We saw that in the last spike.
nina: could we do a hybrid: ephemeral per-tenant IP leases that fall back to shared NAT when pool exhausted? cheaper and still auditable most of the time.
marc: +1 hybrid. The tricky parts: how do we express fallback semantics in the endpoint contract? App owners need deterministic behavior for allowlists.
jordan: exactly — we need a contract that guarantees either (A) stable IP for X days or (B) best-effort ephemeral with explicit fallback.
kevin: proposal sketch: 
```
egress:
  mode: hybrid   # per-tenant-preferred | shared-preferred | forced-per-tenant
  ip_allocation: ephemeral 
  lease_duration: 72h
  fallback: shared-nat
```
This lets ops rotate without breaking allowlists if they expect ephemeral leases.
alyssa: should the default lease_duration be configurable per-tenant? compliance customers might need 30d pinned IPs.
nina: yes, and we need an api flag on the Private controlplane to pin-ip: true/false. On-prem will require a static mode too.
marc: rollout concern: if we flip to hybrid default, many customers could suddenly see different egress paths. We need a canary group and a compatibility header in responses, plus telemetry showing allowlist failures.
sre-bot: deploy:canary started for egress-hybrid 1705804400 — monitoring: egress_ip_changes, external_connect_failures.
jordan: ops question — what observability fields do we need so downstream SREs can debug: tenant_id, allocated_ip, allocation_source, fallback_used?
kevin: +1 to those. Also include route_table_id, eni_id for on-prem/private cases so we can trace mapping.
alyssa: Security: we should document the threat model for shared-nat fallback. Egress filtering and ACLs change semantics if tenant shares IPs.
nina: agree. Also add 'allowlist_grace' in contract: number of days we tolerate allowlist mismatch after fallback before notifying customer.
marc: migration plan idea: 1) implement API flags and telemetry, 2) expose per-tenant pinning in Console, 3) enable hybrid for internal canary tenants, 4) measure allowlist mismatch rate and customer impact, 5) opt-in for customers then opt-out window before forced default.
jordan: can someone sketch a minimal schema for the endpoint contract we can add to the RFC follow-up doc? Something that fits both Hosted and Private controlplanes.
kevin: happy to. Minimal fields: mode, lease_duration, pin_requested, fallback_behavior, telemetry_tags. I'll send a PR.
alyssa: action: add security appendix about shared-nat leakage and mitigation.
nina: action: add e2e test for on-prem static-mode where customers require pinned IPs and HSM integration remains unaffected.
marc: putting this on the next arch sync agenda. cc @kevin @nina for PRs.
jordan: thanks — seems like hybrid default with clear contracts + long-pin override for compliance is the consensus for now.
kevin: filing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/XXXXX
alyssa: note: make sure Console UI shows "egress pinning status" and last_ip_change timestamp.
marc: and we should emit an event to account owners when fallback_used = true so they can proactively adjust allowlists.
sre-bot: note: follow-ups created: #egress-contracts, #egress-metrics, #egress-canary (internal).
